ruleName: SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

Healthcare patient-portal blood-pressure intake. Side-by-side Systolic (value 118, normal) and Diastolic (value 135, out of range) number inputs. The error 'Diastolic must be between 40 and 120 mmHg.' is placed in the Systolic column under the Systolic input, and the Systolic input carries the red alert border; the out-of-range Diastolic has no message. No aria-describedby.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

RTL Arabic (lang=ar dir=rtl) membership address form. A 2-column x 3-row CSS grid holds Postal code (column 1, value 11564, flagged red) and City (column 2, empty). The postal-code error is placed by explicit coordinates into grid-column 2 row 3 — the City column's message slot — so on screen it sits under the empty City input. No aria-describedby.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message contradicts the field's retained value, failing to correctly identify the error.
The city input field is not in an error state, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.

ruleName: Long-form policy article: an inline glossary-term tooltip (Emissions Trading System) opens downward on hover/focus with no Esc dismiss, landing on the first ~3 lines of the next body paragraph. Method 2 absent, so Method 1 is the only path — and it obscures meaningful body text.

Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Retail account signup re-displayed after a failed submit; the email field holds a malformed address (jane.summit.example.com, no @) and the sole per-field error indicator is an error icon carrying a non-empty but uselessly generic alt="error".

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the 'Full name' field, so there is no error identification to evaluate for this control.
The email field error is indicated only by visual styling and an icon with generic alt text 'error' without any text identifying the specific problem.
The password input field is not in an error state, so 3.3.1 Error Identification does not apply to this control.

ruleName: Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

PASSING counter-fixture. Higher-ed LMS reading with a '[1]' footnote reference that opens a citation popup on hover AND keyboard focus, deliberately overlapping the paragraph below (so Method 1 is not relied on). A document-level Escape handler hides the popup while focus REMAINS on the '[1]' button, and activating the trigger also toggles it closed — both SCR39-allowed dismissals.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered glossary tooltip remains visible without self-withdrawing while the trigger is held.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains visible for the duration of the hover and does not automatically dismiss itself on a timer.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): auction 'place a bid' form with the IDENTICAL red border + tint on the email field, but the error is also identified and described in text ('Email address is not valid.') tied via aria-describedby, with aria-invalid='true' and the decorative icon aria-hidden. Should pass.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated for the 'Your name' field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.
The error on the email address field is clearly identified in text and programmatically associated with the input.
No error was demonstrated or flagged for the maximum bid field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to it.

ruleName: SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

CONTROL / discrimination foil (PASS). Event-ticketing phone field, post-submit error state — near-identical component to case-01. The retained value is '(202) 555-CALL', which genuinely contains parentheses, a space, a dash, and the letters C-A-L-L. The field is digits-only and the visible associated error reads 'Phone number must contain only digits. Remove the letters, spaces, and parentheses (for example, enter 2025550143).' — a cause that DID occur and correctly describes this value's actual defect.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is identified and clearly described in text directly beneath the invalid field and programmatically associated via aria-describedby.

ruleName: Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

SaaS 'set your password' screen, post-submit error state. Password field holds a 12-character value (shown as 12 bullets); the visible associated error reads 'Password must be at least 8 characters.' The page's own requirements checklist marks 'At least 8 characters' as MET (green) and 'At least one number' as the only UNMET rule (red). The error asserts a length rule already passed; the actual unmet rule (digit) triggered rejection but is not the one described, so the error contradicts the page's own checklist.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the error by stating the password must be at least 8 characters, contradicting the retained 14-character input.

ruleName: Cedar Mutual Auto 3-step quote wizard silently advanced to 'Step 3 of 3, Review & buy' after an invalid ZIP ('0', too short) on Step 1 was swallowed — Step 2 (coverage options) was skipped because the rating engine had no usable ZIP. The review summary freezes the invalid ZIP '0' as read-only text and shows a placeholder premium '$—'; no error text appears. Cross-page silent-advance variant. LONG-TAIL; content-domain insurance quote wizard, APG stepper + dl review, lazy-validation persona.

CONTROL (discrimination boundary): the same Riverbend Library membership flow as case-01, but the genuine SUCCESS result after VALID input (Age 34, a real email). The server accepted the data and rendered a true confirmation — a read-only summary of the accepted values, a real membership number (RVB-2026-08831), and next steps — with no editable form re-displayed and legitimately no error message. Must be judged passed while case-01..05 are failed.

Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

RTL Arabic e-commerce product page: a size-guide tooltip authored with physical left:0 does not mirror under dir=rtl and opens on top of its own trigger button, covering the label 'دليل المقاسات'. No Esc dismiss. Obscures the trigger itself — FAIL.

Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the error by instructing the user to remove letters and parentheses, even though the field contains only digits.

ruleName: Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. The reveal is the selector abbr.term:hover .bubble with no JS, so keyboard focus structurally cannot reveal it; the author also set tabindex="-1", removing the <abbr> from the tab order.

E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

Government DMV registration-renewal wizard: focus-triggered help bubbles (role=tooltip) under the Plate and VIN fields. A single global setInterval(...,5000) clears any visible bubble every 5 seconds, so the VIN help vanishes while the field still has focus and the user is mid-task. Verified: visible on focus -> display:none at 6s while document.activeElement is still #vin.

Bank reset-password screen redisplayed after rejecting a reused password; the field shows a red outline + a red CSS ::before key glyph and carries aria-invalid='true', but emits NO error text, aria-errormessage, or aria-describedby — nothing in words states what is wrong or why.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The invalid input field is visually flagged with a red border and aria-invalid='true', but no error text is provided to identify the problem.
No error was demonstrated for the 'Confirm new password' field.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake form: a 'What's this?' help popover on the Insurance Member ID field opens down-right with no Esc dismiss and overlaps the next field's required asterisk + label (Patient date of birth) and the input being filled.

BOUNDARY PASS. Community-garden waitlist form with stacked Full name (valid), Email (value 'priya.nair@', invalid), Phone (valid). The error 'Email address is incomplete — add the part after the @.' is rendered inside the Email field's own block directly under the Email input, which carries the red invalid border. There is NO aria-describedby — identification rests entirely on presentation, done correctly.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was flagged or demonstrated for the Full name field.
The input error is clearly identified and described in text directly adjacent to the invalid field.
The optional phone input field is not in an error state.

ruleName: Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

Community allotment newsletter signup re-rendered after a failed submit; the invalid email field ('tom@') wears a 2px red border + red-tinted background as the SOLE error cue. No message, no aria-invalid, no hidden text anywhere conveys that an error occurred.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was flagged or demonstrated for this specific form field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the course input field, making WCAG 3.3.1 error identification not applicable to this control.
The field is visually flagged in an error state with a red border and background tint, but no text identifies or describes the error.

ruleName: Conference call-for-papers form returned after a blank required 'Talk title'; the only error/required cue is the label turned red with a trailing CSS ::after asterisk. No message, no legend explaining the asterisk, no required/aria-required/aria-invalid.

ruleName: Credit-union online-banking enrolment: red role=alert summary states 'Password must be at least 10 characters and include a number', but the Password field is valid (green, aria-invalid=false, meets the rule). rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was detected or demonstrated for the Username field.

ruleName: Homeware ecommerce checkout (en-GB); shipping postcode 9021 is too short and billing postcode SW1A 0AA! has an illegal character, but both reuse one SVG sprite and both <svg role=img> wrappers carry the identical hardcoded aria-label="Invalid input".

ruleName: Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip content remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on an automatic timer.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains visible while the trigger element is held, persisting without self-withdrawing on a timer.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field retains '03/14/2027', which already conforms exactly to MM/DD/YYYY. The visible associated error reads 'Date of birth is invalid. Please use the MM/DD/YYYY format.' — naming a constraint that is already satisfied. The actual error (a birth date set in the future) is never described, so the only guidance is a no-op fix.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No input error was detected or demonstrated for the Legal name field.
The error message misidentifies the error by instructing the user to format the date as MM/DD/YYYY when the entered date already matches that format.

ruleName: SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip content remains visible and persistent while the trigger is held, without automatically withdrawing itself.
The hover-revealed tooltip content remains persistent and does not automatically dismiss or withdraw itself while the trigger is held.

ruleName: Hotel booking review, post-submit error state. Check-in '2026-08-01', check-out '2026-09-25' (55 nights — check-out IS after check-in). The check-out field's visible associated error reads 'Check-out date must be after your check-in date.' — a relation that already holds. The form's own visible policy states 'Maximum stay: 30 nights'; the real, undescribed error is that a 55-night stay exceeds that cap.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Check-in field is not in an error state or flagged as invalid, so error identification does not apply to this element.
The error message contradicts the entered dates by claiming the check-out date must be after the check-in date when it already is.

ruleName: Alumni reunion RSVP (en-GB); email ravi@@pembury.ac.uk (double @) and date 2024-07-18 (in the past) are both invalid, but a refactor cut-and-pasted the date row's error icon above the email row without updating it, so the email field sits beside an SVG whose aria-label="Date is in the past" — correct cause for the wrong field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was demonstrated or flagged for the 'Full name' field, so 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this control.

The field is marked as invalid with a red border and aria-invalid attribute, but the error is not identified in text.

ruleName: GOV.UK council-tax reduction form: top-of-form red error summary announces 'We found 2 errors' and lists Full name + Email, but both render filled and unflagged; the only field actually in error (Telephone, value 'ring me weekdays') has a red border, inline message and aria-invalid=true and is never named. Wrong count AND wrong fields named.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary incorrectly reports an error for the Full name field, which is not flagged in error on the form.
The error summary misidentifies the form errors by omitting the invalid telephone field and incorrectly listing errors for the valid name and email fields.

ruleName: Home-insurance quote wizard, step 2 Property: red role=alert summary says 'Please fix 2 things: Country must be selected. Year the property was built must be a 4-digit year'. Year built is genuinely flagged (value 'nineteen eighty'), but the Country control is a disabled <select> pre-set to 'United Kingdom' (locked because the product is UK-only) — greyed, non-focusable, no aria-invalid — and could not have produced input nor be corrected.

ruleName: City government primary nav: a 'Residents & Services' submenu opens on hover and on activation/focus of its toggle and covers the page banner and intro text. It carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls, but the only way it closes is a document-level click outside the menu (pointer only) — no Escape handler and activating the toggle only re-opens it, so keyboard/magnifier users cannot dismiss the obscuring panel without moving focus away.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No additional content or tooltip appears on hover or focus of the Government navigation item.
